notes: The booklet is a single small image per step, so positions and some rests_on are my best reconstruction. I could not confirm every piece's exact cell from the images.

Step numbering: main steps 1-4, then the 3-step front sub-assembly (5, 6, 7), then main steps 5-9 as steps 8-12. Piece steps in the list follow this order, but several pieces are ordered loosely (for example p10/p11 in step 9, p9/p12/p13/p16 in step 10).
Wheel arches, the 4x4 roof plate and the bracket heights are approximated: arches are treated as 3 plates tall and the bracket as 3 plates tall.

The front bracket p2 carries the side-handle plates p3/p4, the clip plates p25/p26, the clear round plates p33/p34 and the grille tile p1. p3, p4, p25, p26, p33 and p34 are attached sideways, so their position is null.
Wheels p29-p32 and tyres p35-p38 sit on the wheel holders p27/p28 and have no grid position.

Two separate groups is correct for this set, so I kept it. The booklet builds two independent models: the lime-and-red mailbox (steps 1-3) and the flower stand with its roof and heart (steps 4-14). The final page shows them standing side by side with Stephanie, and no step joins them. Nothing physically clutches between them, so I added no rests_on link.
The mailbox group is p18, p21, p22, p7, p8 and the envelope tile p9. The envelope is linked to the door slot and to the minifigure's hand.
Booklet steps counted: mailbox 1-3, main model 4-9, roof sub-assembly 10-12 (mounted at 13), heart 14. The Stephanie minifigure parts are not in the piece list and are not recorded.
The booklet pictures are small, so many positions, layers and some piece roles are my best estimates.
The white plate p4 is turned and sits in the middle (x1-2, y0-3). The two 3x1 slopes p19 and p20 stand on the left and right (x0 and x3) and both rest on p1 and p3. No pieces overlap.
Assumed the 3x1 slopes carry the two cones at their back ends. The gold supports go on the cones. The roof plate p5 sits on both gold supports.
Assumed the mailbox uses the two dark-pink 2x1 slopes (p7, p8) on the red box, and the roof sub-assembly uses the four cheese slopes (p23-p26).
Assumed the heart is two red 3x2 plates (p11, then p10 flipped on top) resting on the white 1x1 side-stud brick p36.
The door p22 is treated as hinged or slotted into the red box p21 and has no grid position.
The cones have only an anti-stud port in the catalogue, so rests_on for the gold supports on the cones is by stacking.
